nodes.question: How do ecosystem properties compare to thermal and water management in GI systems?
nodes.answer: Ecosystem properties are more passive compared to thermal and water management in GI systems.
nodes.paragraph: For effective water management in GI projects, integrated green-grey infrastructure systems are recommended. To achieve ther - mal objectives, insulation materials are pivotal. The ecosystem properties are more pas- sive as compared to thermal and water management; hence, specific considerations must be accorded to ensure GI success. The key contribution of the study was the delineation of the key multifunctional factors that support GI adoption and implementation success in developing regions. Keywords Green infrastructure Multifunctionality Climate change Environmental sustainability Built environment Extended author information available on the last page of the article S. Seidu et al. 1 Introduction Scientists contend that greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions are rising despite worldwide attempts to limit them under the Kyoto Protocol, a UN programme (Koh, 2018). In the same vein, pressing global environmental issues include climate change. Recent stud- ies have shown that green infrastructure (GI) systems can be a useful policy tool for tackling these complex issues (Owusu-Manu et al., 2023; Seidu et al., 2024). In several scholarly works, the concept of GI has gained momentum over the past decades.
